reported.text: Return the substring(s) nested deepest inside (), [] or {} brackets, e.g., 'abc(def[ghi]jkl)mno' gives ['ghi'].

sources.passage:
Bloomberg | Technical Phone Interview | Entry Level - SWE
Interviewer was nice. They asked me questions about my background, asked me about the projects I worked on. Then, they asked me the following technical question which was along the lines of: "Given a string, find the deepest string nested inside a '()', '[]' or '{}'."

e.g.
'''
"abc(def)ghi" => ["def"]
"abc(def[ghi]jkl)mno" => ["ghi"]
"abc(def)ghi[jkl]mno" => ["def", "jkl"]
"abc" => ["abc"]
"" => [""]
(),[],{}
'''

reported.text: Given a Connect Four board and the next player, report whether someone has already won or whether the next player can win with one move (harder than Tic-Tac-Toe state validation).

sources.passage:
Bloomberg Phone Screen question
Hi everyone,
  Had an interview with Bloomberg. And they asked a question simlar to Leetcode 794. But it is harder.
  The question is to check the current status of Connect 4 game board, and to return if who wins without any moves or one of the players can win with the next move. The input is board(2D array), and the next player. 
  For example, in the first board below, yellow wins. In the second board below, whoever plays the next chip wins.
   Please help! Thank you!

reported.text: Given a dictionary and a set of letters, return the longest dictionary word that can be formed from those letters (order does not matter).

sources.passage:
Bloomberg | Phone, 1st round, Hackerrank | Scrabble
Interviewing for senior software engineer, recruiter reached out on linkedin.

This was the first technical round with hackrrank coding questions, 1 hour. The problem was pretty complex and haven't seen this in leetcode tagged with bloomberg. Not sure if this even exists on leetcode.

The question was to find longest matching word from dictionary for given set of chars.
e.g. 
dict={when, what, whatthen, whatnow}, input="whatno", expected output= "what"
dict={when, what, whatthen, whatnow}, input="whatnwo", expected output= "whatnow"
dict={when, what, whatthen, whatnow}, input="wonthaw", expected output= "whatnow"

I solved it using trie and I was able to get output for given test cases but I later realized the logic fails for input like 3rd case mentioned above.

Haven't heard back yet, hoping for the best.

            Create a function that returns true or false

reported.text: Implement your own resizable list class with O(1) indexed access that can grow dynamically; discuss how much extra capacity to allocate and why.

sources.passage:
Bloomberg SDE Intern Interview Experience
I applied through a referral from a campus recruiter. Directly got a mail to schedule my interview. The round 1 interviewer was a person from the Pune office. Both the rounds were online.

Round 1: 

- Asked about my introduction ( They want to check the graduation year and if applying for correct role ), why I wanted to join Bloomberg
- Brief discussion over array and implementation of linked list. Was asked about to implement my own linked list class.
    - Conditions
        1. Must have 0(1) access
        2. Should be able to allocate new memory and change the size dynamically.
- She asked my how much extra memory I would allocate and why. I gave a interesting answer, stating to use a simple learning algorithm which would eventually learn and allocate the memory as per users requirements in the past.
- Coding question: [Maximum Nesting Depth of the Parentheses - LeetCode](https://leetcode.com/problems/maximum-nesting-depth-of-the-parentheses/description/) . Only change was I had to return all pairs of indices ( starting and ending ) of all the maximum depth pairs.
- The question takes place on hackerearth/hackerrank platform, but they do not compile the code and only dry run.
- Discussion over which data-structure to use for a telephone lookup, should be efficient both ways. Lookup by Name and Phone Number too.

Round 2:

- After a month, I again was asked to book an interview slot.
- This time there were 2 people, both from the London office. ( Had some issue understanding what they were exactly saying due to the accent )
- Was asked about my previous internship experience in detail, about my role what I liked, what I exactly did, what was my role. Same about my one of the project I had mentioned in my resume.
- Jumped to the coding question:
    - There are trades coming in the market like
        - AAPL 500
        - MSFT 200
        - AMZ 100
        - MSFT 400
    - Efficiently search the total quantity of trades for a particular stock, and also find out the k most frequently traded stocks. Top K stocks at any particular moment. ( Like after a request for top k stocks, new stocks can be added )
- Then asked me about what unit testing is and there implementation.

Was sent a rejection mail a day latter.

reported.text: Given banks with operating hours and a transaction time, decide whether the transaction is valid.

sources.passage:
Bloomberg technical interview questions
There are 2 technical rounds in Bloomberg software development intern process.Round 1 is the technical round of easy difficulty and Round 2 is the technical round of medium - hard difficulty.
Round 1:
There are banks X,Y,Z and with their operational timings 
We have been provided with a transaction time and we have to determine whether the transaction is valid or not.
I am able to solve this question and I got mail for the second technical round.

Round 2:
Two questions were asked in this round .
First one is:

https://leetcode.com/problems/decode-string/description/?orderBy=hot

I am able to solve this after two/three attempts and then the interviewer gave me another question.

Second one is:
This is a hard level question and it asked to calculate the minimum path sum in a binary tree.
It's just exactly opposite to the given below question, just replace max with min.

https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-maximum-path-sum/

I was able to solve it partially and more than that I wasn't able to communicate my approach to the interviewer.

And after this I got a rejection mail,focus on clearing your basics they aren't much focused on optimized or best solution as they don't run on editior.
